patch.value: The graph audit raises duplicate dependency rows at warning severity and the only remediation available deletes every copy, so collapsing a duplicate means briefly destroying a real edge

The graph audit reports duplicate_dependency_row at warning severity, the highest severity it emits, and the mutation surface has no operation that resolves it. Reproduced end to end on this workspace during the 2026-07-28 review pass.

Setup. pm-dkrmzv carried two identical rows toward the same target: pm-nfrhf0 implements at 04:20:29 and pm-nfrhf0 implements at 10:02:34. Same source, same target, same kind. The audit correctly flagged it as duplicate_dependency_row with severity warning.

Attempted remediation. pm update pm-dkrmzv --dep-remove id=pm-nfrhf0,kind=implements. The documented selector grammar for dep-remove is id or id=<id>,kind=<value>,source_kind=<value>, which is the most precise selector the flag accepts. It removed both rows. The item was left with no implements edge toward pm-nfrhf0 at all, and the audit went clean by deleting a real relationship rather than by collapsing a duplicate.

Recovery required a second mutation to re-add the edge, so the workspace passed through a state where a relationship the graph depends on did not exist, and the history now records a removal and an addition rather than a deduplication. On a workspace where an agent is repairing many duplicates in one pass, or where another agent reads the graph between the two writes, that window is not academic.

The gap is precise. Selector semantics are defensible on their own terms: a selector selects every match, and remove-all is what a selector should do. The defect is that this is the only remediation offered for a condition the audit raises at warning severity, so the tool asks for a repair it provides no safe operation to perform. Every other governance finding this project raises has a remediation path that does not pass through deleting correct data.

Three shapes would close it, in increasing generality. A dedupe intent on the mutation surface that collapses identical rows to one and is a no-op when there is nothing to collapse. An occurrence-scoped selector so a specific row can be named. Or write-time idempotence for exact-duplicate dependency rows, which would prevent the condition rather than remediate it, and would also mean the audit finding could only ever describe legacy data.

The last option deserves weight. This duplicate was created by an ordinary append: the edge already existed from an earlier pass, a later pass appended the same edge again, and nothing objected. update --dep appending is correct and deliberate behaviour for distinct rows. Appending a byte-identical row is the case where append and idempotence disagree, and the audit already declares which side it is on by calling the result a warning.

Boundaries. pm-rggtvd owns hierarchy-canonicalizing kinds bypassing cycle detection, which is a different write-time canonicalization problem. pm-4020c5 owns the fragmented kind lexicon. pm-6x7o owns the governance audit's own scope. None of them owns the absence of a safe remediation for a finding the audit already raises.

A duplicate dependency row can be collapsed to one in a single mutation without the workspace ever passing through a state where the edge is absent; Either exact-duplicate dependency rows are rejected or deduplicated at write time, or an occurrence-scoped remediation exists, and the choice is documented; The remediation is a no-op when there is nothing to collapse, so it is safe to run across a whole workspace; A regression test creates an exact-duplicate row, remediates it, and asserts the edge survives with exactly one row; The audit finding text names the remediation operation

message: Reproduced live during the 2026-07-28 review pass on pm-dkrmzv, which held two identical implements rows toward pm-nfrhf0 created 04:20:29 and 10:02:34. The documented id+kind selector on dep-remove removed both and required a second mutation to restore the relationship. value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text:
Refinement from a live repair on 2026-08-03, narrowing this finding rather than restating it.

I reproduced the duplicate-row condition by accident (adding related pm-q91qyd to pm-ki67py, which already carried that exact edge) and then repaired it. The repair did not require destroying both copies: --dep-remove accepts id=<id>,kind=<value>,source_kind=<value>, and the two rows differed in source_kind (cli:create:dep vs cli:update:dep), so the newer one was removable on its own. The audit went from 12 findings back to the 11-finding baseline with the original edge intact and no interval during which the relationship was absent.

So the destructive-remediation problem is real but narrower than stated: it applies to rows that are identical in all three selector dimensions, not to every duplicate the audit reports. The audit's own sample line already prints the pair without the discriminator, which is why the remediation reads as all-or-nothing - 'pm-ki67py -> pm-q91qyd (related x2)' does not say the two rows are separable.

Two consequences for this item's scope. First, the sample should print the discriminating fields when they differ, so the reader can see whether a precise removal exists. Second, the genuinely unrepairable case is duplicate rows agreeing on id, kind and source_kind, and that is the population worth counting - the current count conflates it with the separable case.

value.text:
Recurrence confirmed 2026-08-07, and the class is now ratcheted.

The finding returned. Three exactly duplicated rows were present on active holders: pm-cg1sjb toward pm-ei6x66 and toward pm-zlv8jl, and pm-ei6x66 toward pm-rtn5h6, all kind related. Every duplicate carries source_kind cli:update:dep with created_at on 2026-08-05, so they were minted by dependency-appending mutations during an enrichment pass over items that already held the same edge. The original reproduction on 2026-07-28 used pm-dkrmzv and a different kind, so this is a second independent occurrence of the same write-time behaviour rather than surviving damage.

The destructive repair reproduced exactly as described. Removing with the most precise selector the flag accepts deleted both copies and left the holder with no edge toward the target, verified by reading the dependency list immediately afterwards. Restoring required a second mutation, so each of the three repairs passed through a state where a real relationship did not exist, and the history now records three removals and three additions rather than three deduplications. Six mutations to collapse three duplicates.

The class is now enforced. A graph_finding selector source was added to the tracker measurement ratchet and duplicate_dependency_row is declared with a ceiling of zero, owned by this item, so a fresh duplicate fails the gate before merge instead of waiting for a reviewer to read the audit. The source is exhaustive, so an undeclared audit finding code also surfaces. This does not substitute for the acceptance criteria here: the ratchet catches the row after it is written, and the criteria ask for the write to be idempotent or for an occurrence-scoped remediation to exist. It only removes the silence between the write and the discovery.

Live repository audit also reports zero duplicate_dependency_row findings. Linked mutation and audit tests passed 29/29.

Touching an exact dependency identity preserves the first provenance row and atomically normalizes all duplicates to one; a repeated add remains one row; temporary acceptance and live graph audit report zero duplicate findings.
